title: add fragment-sentinel handshake and ordered toolcall resume to SSE stream
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background and motivation: We observed two classes of production failures when long-running streaming responses interleave function/tool call sentinels with delayed fragments: 1) partial JSON emitted to the client due to chunk boundary cuts inside a tool-call sentinel, and 2) tool-call events replayed out of order on resume after transient connection resets. This PR implements a lightweight in-band handshake (fragment-sentinel ACK) and a small resume protocol that ensures ordered handoff of function/tool call events without adding a separate control channel.

What this change does: Adds a 3-part solution: 1) fragment sentinel handshake — an in-stream ACK marker emitted at the end of a logically complete JSON span to guarantee clients can identify safe cut points; 2) prefix-stable chunker — reworks the SSE chunker to prefer emitting whole UTF-8 and JSON token boundaries and to hold half-token fragments until a matching sentinel/ACK arrives or a short timeout elapses; 3) ordered toolcall resume — on reconnect the client/server exchange includes the last-ack sequence id so the server can replay or skip function/toolcall events deterministically, preserving original ordering and avoiding duplicate handoffs.

Compatibility and scope: This is scoped to the OpenAI-compat streaming layer and the server-side SSE reassembly path. No changes to the public REST generation endpoints. The handshake marker is backward-compatible: older clients will treat the sentinel as opaque data but will benefit indirectly because boundary fragmentation is reduced.

Checklist: - [x] implement fragment sentinel emission at stream flush points - [x] update SSE chunker to hold partial UTF-8/JSON tokens and prefer whole-token emission - [x] implement in-band resume sequence negotiation and deterministic replay/skip logic - [x] add unit + integration tests covering partial JSON cases and reconnect replay - [x] benchmark critical path to ensure <5% median latency impact under typical loads - [x] docs: add short compatibility note in streaming section

Commits (summary): - 8d2a1f0: add sentinel marker generation and seq id emission - b7f4c3a: prefix-stable chunker rewrite with boundary holdback logic - d2e9f44: resume handshake and deterministic replay engine - 3f5b6ab: tests for partial-json-rescue and toolcall-ordering - 9a7d2be: integration test harness tweak for flaky network simulation - a1b4c55: update streaming docs and changelog entry

Files changed (high level): - streaming/sse/chunker.go: implement prefix-stable chunker and holdback queues - streaming/sse/sentinel.go: sentinel marker encode/decode and seq id management - streaming/sse/resume_handler.go: negotiation and replay/skip policy - streaming/sse/handlers_test.go: new partial-json + resume tests - docs/openai_compat/streaming.md: compatibility note and handshake description - telemetry/metrics.yaml: add sentinel_emitted counter and resume_replay histogram - api/compat/fixtures/toolcall-replay.json: test fixtures

Review conversation (high level): - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "This addresses the root cause we saw in the incident. I'm concerned about the timeout heuristics in the chunker — can we ensure the holdback does not increase p95 under load?" - Maya Chen (author): "Added a micro-benchmark and tuned the default holdback window to 12ms; included guard so chunker bypasses holdback for very small payloads (<=32 bytes). Benchmarks included in PR." - Lina Voss (reviewer): "Two nits on comments and one on variable naming in chunker.go. Also requested explicit test for UTF-8 multi-byte char split case." - Maya Chen: "Addressed nits, added utf8_split_test, and clarified comments. PTAL." - Diego Morales (approver): "Verified integration tests and replay determinism locally; CI passed — approving."

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (network-flaky profile): pass after re-run - lint: pass with one minor gofmt fix applied in the branch - perf-check: pass (median generation latency +3.1%, p95 +4.7% in sandbox; within target)

Notes on design tradeoffs: The in-band sentinel avoids a second control plane and reduces operational surface, but requires careful encoding to remain opaque for older clients. We chose a compact 12-byte sentinel with a 64-bit seq id and an 16-bit flags field. The chunker timeout is conservative; operators can tune via STREAM_CHUNKER_HOLDBACK_MS.

Release notes: "Fix streaming boundary and resume behavior: reduce partial JSON emissions on SSE streams and guarantee ordered replay/skip of function/tool-call events on reconnects. Backward-compatible in-band sentinel used; operators may tune STREAM_CHUNKER_HOLDBACK_MS if necessary."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green. Deployed to canary cluster for one week and monitored metrics (sentinel_emitted and resume_replay) before wide rollout.
